speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned suffering from a chronic cough and recurrent bronchitis; to begin my assessment, how long have you had these symptoms, and do you smoke?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is a very long duration for symptoms, and the fact that you are a non-smoker despite producing copious yellow-green sputum is notable. To differentiate this from chronic bronchitis and assess for bronchiectasis, have you ever undergone a high-resolution CT scan of your chest, and do you experience hemoptysis (coughing up blood)?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Aggressive cough with thick, yellow-green sputum. I also have Cough worse in the morning, History of recurrent bronchitis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis. The clinical presentation of chronic cough with copious purulent sputum for 11 years, morning predominance, and recurrent bronchitis in a non-smoker is classic for this condition, likely caused by post-infectious damage or an underlying immune deficiency.
